answer: Chained Quota Attrition**: Each identity must complete a random draw of real work tasks whose results are cross-verified against a rotating panel. A basalt-like fixed schedule assigns each new identity a shrinking task quota. Duplicate behavioral fingerprints (timing, phrasing) trigger quota halving. A juniper tier of trusted reviewers samples outputs, and rejected clones forfeit their compute deposit plus queue position. An ocean of waiting tasks must be cleared before payout. Cloning costs grow superlinearly while rewards stay flat, making marginal clones negative-EV.
